claim: Dénia Castle costs EUR 3 adult / EUR 2 students-seniors / EUR 1 children 8-16 (under 8 and residents free); sits 60m on a hilltop with panoramic Mediterranean views; pedestrian-only access; ~2-3 hour visit.
quote: Adults: €3 ... Students/Seniors/Groups (25+): €2 ... Children (8–16): €1 ... Under 8: Free ... The 60-meter hilltop location offers panoramic vistas of Dénia.

claim: Castle opening hours are seasonal: Nov-Mar 10:00-18:00, Apr-May 10:00-19:00, June 10:00-19:30, Jul-Aug 10:00-20:30, Sep 10:00-20:00, Oct 10:00-19:30, with occasional summer night visits to 00:30.
quote: November–March: 10:00 AM–6:00 PM ... July–August: 10:00 AM–8:30 PM ... Summer evenings occasionally extend to 12:30 AM for special nighttime visits.

claim: Inside the castle the Renaissance Palau del Governador (c.1600) housed the archaeological museum; notable features include the Mig Tower with double horseshoe arches and the Portal de la Vila entrance.
quote: Governor's Palace (Palau del Governador): This Renaissance structure from around 1600 ... The Mig Tower with double horseshoe arches ... Portal de la Vila entrance

claim: The Dénia Archaeological Museum relocated from the castle to Casa de la Marquesa (Calle Cavallers 3) downtown in October 2024, admission is free, and it covers four periods: Iberian, Roman (Dianium), Islamic (Taifa of Daniya) and Christian (13th-18th c.).
quote: The museum relocated to Casa de la Marquesa (Calle Cavallers, 3) in October 2024 ... Entrance to the Archaeological Museum is free ... Iberian ... Roman ... Islamic ... Christian

claim: Archaeological Museum hours: Mon-Sat 10:00-14:00 and 16:00-19:00, Sun 09:00-15:00; closed Dec 25, Jan 1, Mar 19 and May 1.
quote: Monday-Saturday: 10 AM–2 PM, 4 PM–7 PM ... Sunday: 9 AM–3 PM ... Closed: December 25, January 1, March 19, May 1

claim: Les Roques is the old quarter preserving the Arab medina with narrow pedestrian streets and is the gateway to the castle; Loreto Street is the most emblematic pedestrian thoroughfare, dense with restaurants and tapas bars.
quote: the Les Roques neighborhood, described as preserving "the essence of the Arab medina" ... Loreto Street stands as the most emblematic thoroughfare, completely pedestrianized ... high concentration of restaurants and tapas bars

claim: Baix la Mar is the photogenic 16th-century fishing quarter with low brightly-coloured houses and squares (Sant Antoni, Creu); fishing boats return to the port from 4 PM, and the Calle Marqués de Campo boulevard is lined with centuries-old plane trees.
quote: Baix la Mar ... "low houses in bright colors and charming squares, such as Sant Antoni or Creu" ... fishing activity visible from 4 PM onward ... Calle Marqués de Campo ... "centuries-old plane trees"

claim: Cova de l'Aigua sits on Montgó's north face at ~350m; the PR-CV 152 trail from Ermita del Pare Pere runs 30-45 minutes one-way and the cave (two rooms, a pond, a 238 AD Roman inscription) was used from Iberian times and as an Arab Taifa-era water store.
quote: on the north face of Montgó, about 350 meters high ... PR-CV 152 trail ... lasts between 30 and 45 minutes ... At the entrance there is a Roman inscription dating from 238 AD ... two rooms and a small pond at the bottom

claim: The Cova de l'Aigua circular hike is rated difficult, about 6.15 km / 3.8 miles, taking roughly 2h33m, with some technical and hazardous terrain.
quote: The Cova de l'Aigua - Racó del Bou Trail is a difficult 3.8-mile hike ... the total distance is 6.15 km with an estimated time of 2 hours 33 minutes ... highly technical, difficult, or hazardous terrain

claim: The Cabo de San Antonio lighthouse (built 1861, 17m tall, 175m above sea level) sits where Montgó plunges into the sea on 150m+ cliffs; the adjacent mirador overlooks Xàbia bay and on clear days you can see Ibiza, reached via CV-736 / Carretera del Faro (~4km).
quote: Located 175 metres above sea level, its current construction dates back to 1861 ... 17 meters high ... cliffs of more than 150 meters ... you can see the island of Ibiza when the day is very clear ... about 4km to the lighthouse

claim: Les Rotes is the southern rocky coastline mixing pine and sea, ending at Les Arenetes beach, while Montgó Natural Park is an iconic regional landmark with multi-difficulty hiking routes between Dénia and Jávea.
quote: Les Rotes Coastal Area ... "pinos y casitas de campo" ... Les Arenetes Beach marks the area's end ... Montgó Natural Park ... "todo un icono para la comarca"
